overview: Two basic ways to connect circuit components — one shares a single path, the other offers multiple paths.
genZNote: Series makes everyone share one road. Parallel gives everyone their own lane.

aspects.label: Current Path
aspects.valueA: Single path — same current flows through every component.
aspects.valueB: Multiple paths — current splits across branches.

aspects.label: Voltage Across Components
aspects.valueA: Divides across each component (sums to total EMF).
aspects.valueB: Same across each branch (equal to the source voltage).

aspects.label: Total (Equivalent) Resistance
aspects.valueA: Simple sum of individual resistances (R = R1+R2+...).
aspects.valueB: Reciprocal sum, always less than the smallest individual resistance (1/R = 1/R1+1/R2+...).

aspects.label: Effect of One Component Failing (Open)
aspects.valueA: Breaks the entire circuit — all components stop working.
aspects.valueB: Other branches continue to function normally.
